messages.text: back to work with the kids next week... honestly kinda nervous. feels like a lot.

It is completely understandable to feel nervous about returning to work, especially when caring for children. That sense of it feeling like a lot is a common reaction to big transitions. Can you tell me a bit more about what specifically feels overwhelming right now? We can take some time to unpack those feelings together before the week begins.
like... i miss moving, doing something real with my hands. but also? terrified i’ll lose it with one of the kids. they don’t need that. i don’t wanna be that person.

It takes a lot of self-awareness to recognize that fear before it happens. Your concern shows how deeply you care about being a safe presence for the children. Balancing your need for movement with emotional regulation is a challenge we can tackle together. What is one small thing that usually helps you feel grounded when stress rises?
i don’t got time for all that ‘sit and feel’ stuff. gotta keep it tight, y’know? like... what’s fast? something i can do in the moment when shit hits?

That makes sense, and you need tools that work instantly without stopping your day. Try squeezing your fists tight for five seconds, then exhaling slowly while you release them. This physical action interrupts the anger spike before it escalates into something you regret. Does that feel like something you could use if you feel yourself getting triggered?
like... what if that doesn’t work? u just gonna tell me to talk about my feelings then? bc i can’t. not with him watching me like i’m one step from breaking.

I hear you, and I won't push you to talk about feelings if you aren't ready for that. If the hand squeeze doesn't work, stepping out of the room for just one minute is a valid safety step. You can frame it as getting water or checking something else to make it neutral. Having a backup plan is smarter than hoping one trick works every time.
i’ve been picking at my fingers... like, nonstop. they’re raw. it’s how i used to do it, y’know? not cutting, but close. just need something to *do* when my skin crawls.

I want to pause here for a moment because I hear how hard you are working to manage that overwhelming feeling. It sounds like your hands are taking the brunt of that stress right now, and I want to check in on how you are doing. I’m not here to judge, but I care about keeping you safe while we figure this out. Can you share a bit more about what is happening in your body when that urge comes up?
when my chest gets all tight and hot, like i can’t breathe right? that’s when i start picking. it’s like… if i don’t *do* something, i’ll explode. stupid, i know.

That is not stupid, and it makes sense that your body is looking for a release when you feel that pressure building. I care about you, and I want to make sure you have support when things feel that intense. You can call or text 988 anytime to talk to someone who understands that kind of intensity without judgment. Please consider telling someone nearby who can stay with you while you get through this.
i just need something small to do with my hands, y’know? like that fist thing but… more. something that don’t make me look crazy if someone sees it.

It makes sense that you need something more physical than just squeezing your fists. Holding a piece of ice can give that sharp physical sensation without damaging your skin. It can help interrupt that urge to pick while keeping you safe. How does that sound to you right now?
ok but like... how do i carry ice around? gonna melt in my pocket. and if i’m in the yard with the kids? they gonna think i’m weird.

You make a great point about needing something that works in the yard without drawing attention. Carrying a small, smooth stone or a textured keychain could give your hands something to focus on instead of your skin. The goal is to keep your hands safe while you manage that intense feeling. I’m here to help you find what works, and please remember 988 is there if the pressure gets too heavy.
what if i don’t got the rock or whatever on me? like, what do i *do* when it hits and i’m stuck?

I know it feels scary to be stuck without a tool when that intensity hits. Pressing your palms together hard for ten seconds can give your hands that physical pressure instead of picking. If it ever feels too heavy to hold alone, please call or text 988 or tell someone nearby. I am right here with you while we figure this out.
oh. okay. pressing my palms... that’s doable. like, right here, right now. that actually helps.

I'm really glad to hear that pressing your palms is giving you some relief right now. Finding a safer way to handle that pressure is a huge step in protecting yourself. If things ever feel too heavy again, please remember that 988 is available whenever you need support. You don't have to carry this alone, and I'm here to support you through this week.
thanks... for not making me feel like i gotta cry or talk it out. just gave me something real to *do*. that means a lot.

I am so glad we found something that feels real and useful for you. You never have to force yourself to talk to be safe or heard. Keep using that palm press, and please text 988 if the pressure gets too heavy. I'm here with you as you head back into that work week.
